title: groundstation field test №22: the UK EO DataHub, a fourth catalog
heading: THE FIELD TEST №22
sub: groundstation · 5 prompts · 5 live artifacts · 3 works, 2 partly, 0 not yet · October 30, 2026 · Development Seed labs
lede: UK EO DataHub's open catalog (CEDA's STAC of UK Sentinel ARD and EOCIS products) is now a fourth catalog, beside Earth Search, NASA VEDA and Planetary Computer. Its pixels are public COGs, so the shared tiler draws them with no account. These 5 asks cover what that opens: a UK optical swipe, band math inside a packed 10-band file, radar, a class map and a scaled vegetation product. Not here yet: EODH's commercial imagery (an account), its own tiler (an account) and its NetCDF products (UKCP18, CMIP6, land surface temperature, sea ice), which this render path cannot draw. Run on add-eodh-catalog at 0.69.0.

rounds.name: Round 1: 5 UK asks against the new catalog

cases.prompt: Show me the Somerset Levels this spring and this summer from the UK's own Sentinel-2 data. Is there still floodwater in March?
cases.returned:
search_imagery("eodh", ["sentinel2_ard"], bbox=[-2.95, 51.05, -2.75, 51.17], datetime_range="2026-01-01/2026-03-31", max_cloud_cover=30)

render_map(..., layers=[2026-03-19, 2026-08-13], compare=True)  # no assets passed
  tiles: ...&assets=cog|bidx=3,2,1  (true colour picked from the file's own band list)
  rescale 41,164: 2nd to 98th percentile of the raw values over the box, widest of 2 scenes
cases.answer: No widespread floodwater on 19 March 2026. UK EO DataHub's Sentinel-2 ARD (Defra and JNCC) had a 0.0% cloud scene on 2026-03-19 and a 0.01% one on 2026-08-13, both covering the whole box. The water index (NDWI) stays below zero almost everywhere in March: its 98th percentile is -0.30, so open water is a small fraction of the box, not a flooded moor. The Levels were greener in March than in August: median NDVI 0.784 against 0.522, which reads as grass grown in spring, then cut or dried by late summer. The swipe map shows both dates in true colour.
cases.artifact_label: swipe map: Somerset Levels, 19 March and 13 August 2026 ↗
cases.learning: Works. Two things had to change for this card. EODH's search returns only datetime for each item, so groundstation now asks for the full properties (a fields setting on the catalog's entry) and gets cloud cover back. The cloud filter itself was always applied on EODH's side. And all 10 bands sit in one file, so true colour comes from that file's band list (cog|bidx=3,2,1) without the caller naming bands.
cases.shows: a fourth catalog · cloud cover restored with a STAC fields request · true colour from a packed 10-band file · swipe

cases.prompt: How green is the New Forest in mid October?
cases.returned:
search_imagery("eodh", ["sentinel2_ard"], bbox=[-1.75, 50.80, -1.50, 50.95], datetime_range="2026-08-01/2026-10-21", max_cloud_cover=15)
  recommended: neodc.sentinel_ard.data.sentinel_2.2026.10.17.S2B_20261017_latn510lonw0022_T30UWB_ORB137_20261017131842_utm30n_osgb
  cloud_cover 0.06  covers_aoi_pct 100.0
  reason: clearest (0.1% cloud) and best-covering (100.0% of the area), not a tradeoff
compute_statistics("eodh", "sentinel2_ard", <2026-10-17>, expression="(nir-red)/(nir+red)", bbox=[-1.75, 50.80, -1.50, 50.95])
  min -0.2842  max 0.9184  mean 0.6906  median 0.723  p2 0.3226  p98 0.865  valid 100.0%  description "(cog_Red-cog_Red)/(cog_Red+cog_Red)"
preview_item(..., expression="(nir-red)/(nir+red)", colormap_name="rdylgn")
  ...&expression=(b1-b2)/(b1+b2)&assets=cog|bidx=7,3&rescale=-1,1&colormap_name=rdylgn
cases.answer: Still green: median NDVI 0.723 over the box on 17 October 2026 (0.06% cloud, the whole box covered), with the middle 96% of pixels between 0.32 and 0.86. The low end is the open heath and the villages, the high end the woodland. One thing to weigh: the scene's 0.06% cloud is a figure for the whole tile, and the map shows a scatter of small cumulus over the forest that come out as orange spots in the NDVI. They are a sliver of the box, so they pull the low tail, not the median. The map swipes true colour against NDVI.
cases.artifact_label: map: New Forest true colour and NDVI, 17 October 2026 ↗
cases.learning: Works, with a label to ignore and clouds to look for. The expression names nir and red, which are bands inside one file here, not assets. groundstation reads the item's eo:bands and turns them into band 7 and band 3 of that file. The tiler then labels the result (cog_Red-cog_Red)/(cog_Red+cog_Red). That label is wrong and the number is right: the file names its bands Blue, Green, Red, RE_B5, RE_B6, RE_B7, NIR_B8, and a woodland pixel read directly gives red 49, NIR 320, an NDVI of 0.73.
cases.shows: nir and red resolved inside one 10-band file · NDVI number with its spread · index map

cases.prompt: The Sound of Barra on radar, the most recent pass
cases.returned:
search_imagery("eodh", ["sentinel1_ard"], bbox=[-7.45, 57.0, -7.15, 57.15], limit=5)
  2026-07-13  covers 100.0  neodc.sentinel_ard.data.sentinel_1.2026.07.13.S1C_20260713_125_desc_064542_064607_VVVH_G0_GB_OSGB_RTCK_SpkRL
  2026-07-13  covers 100.0  neodc.sentinel_ard.data.sentinel_1.2026.07.13.S1C_20260713_125_desc_064542_064607_VVVH_G0_NI_TM65_RTCK_SpkRL
  2026-07-13  covers 100.0  neodc.sentinel_ard.data.sentinel_1.2026.07.13.S1C_20260713_125_desc_064517_064542_VVVH_G0_GB_OSGB_RTCK_SpkRL
  2026-07-11  covers 100.0  neodc.sentinel_ard.data.sentinel_1.2026.07.11.S1C_20260711_103_asc_181503_181528_VVVH_G0_GB_OSGB_RTCK_SpkRL
compute_statistics(..., assets=["data|bidx=1"], bbox=...)
  min -51.43  max 7.065  mean -26.32  median -27.39  p2 -40.21  p98 -9.739  valid 79.94%  description "data_b1"
cases.answer: The newest radar pass over Barra in this catalog is 13 July 2026, 3.5 months old, while its Sentinel-2 runs to 21 October. Radar sees through the Hebridean cloud, and the VV backscatter shows it: median -27.4 dB over the box, water and sand flats dark (the 2nd percentile is -40.2 dB), land and rock brighter (98th percentile -9.7 dB). 80% of the box has data, and the rest falls outside the swath.
cases.artifact_label: map: Sound of Barra, Sentinel-1 VV backscatter, 13 July 2026 ↗
cases.learning: Partly. The scene renders and the numbers are in dB, but 3 things needed a person. Sentinel-1 ARD stops at 2026-07-15 here, so most recent means summer, not this week. Its single data asset lists no bands, so VV had to be picked by index (data|bidx=1), from the item's sar:polarization order. And each pass comes twice, on a GB grid and on an Irish grid, and the search returns both.
cases.shows: Sentinel-1 ARD in dB · band picked by index when no band list exists · catalog freshness gap

cases.tag: a class map with its legend
cases.prompt: What covers the Cairngorms around Glenmore and Aviemore?
cases.returned:
search_imagery("eodh", ["eocis-chuk-geospatial-landcover"], bbox=[-3.9, 57.0, -3.5, 57.15])
  recommended: 852e5728-b78f-49dc-9fc1-8e65d8bd6b52
  cloud_cover None  covers_aoi_pct 100.0
  reason: best-covering scene at 100.0% of the area; this collection reports no cloud cover
compute_statistics(..., assets=["data"], bbox=...)
  min 1  max 21  mean 9.644  median 9  p2 2  p98 12  valid 100.0%  description "data_Land cover"
  unique 10
file tags: flag_values "[-1 1 2 ... 21]"  flag_meanings "No_data Deciduous_woodland Coniferous_woodland Arable ... Heather Heather_grassland Bog ..."
render_map(..., colormap_name="ukceh-landcover")  -> legend "UKCEH Land Cover", 21 classes
cases.answer: Mostly heather: class 9 (Heather) is both the median and the most common value over the box, in EOCIS's 100 m land cover for 2023. 10 classes are present, and the middle 96% of pixels run from class 2 (coniferous woodland, the Glenmore and Rothiemurchus forests) to class 12 (inland rock, the high plateau). The map draws each class in the colour the file itself declares, with the legend.
cases.artifact_label: map: Cairngorms land cover 2023, UKCEH classes ↗
cases.learning: Works. The class names and colours ship in the GeoTIFF's tags, not in STAC, so they went into groundstation's legend list once. The public tiler only knows its own colormap names, so any legend in that list now goes to it as an explicit value-to-colour map. Class -1 is No_data and is left out, so it draws clear.
cases.shows: categorical layer · file's own class colours as a legend · reused legend list

describe_collection("eodh", "eocis-chuk-land-vegetation-lai")
  description: "... Gap-filled data are available for 100m spatial resolution at a 15-day temporal resolution.  The data must be divided by a scaling factor of 20."
  extent.temporal: 2018-04-01 to 2024-12-31
compute_statistics(..., assets=["data"], bbox=...)
  min 0  max 129  mean 39.89  median 39  p2 2  p98 86  valid 100.0%  description "data_lai_leaf_index"
cases.answer: A median leaf area index of about 2.0 for the 15 days to 23 August 2024: the raw median is 39 and the collection says to divide by 20. The middle 96% runs from 0.1 to 4.3, which is harvested fields at the low end and Thetford Forest's pines at the high end. The map draws the raw values, which keeps the pattern and needs no scaling.
cases.artifact_label: map: East Anglia leaf area index, August 2024 ↗
cases.learning: Partly. The scale factor is only in the collection's prose, not in raster:bands, so the tool returns raw numbers and the division was done by reading the description. The product also ends in December 2024, so it describes past seasons, not this one.
cases.shows: 15-day 100 m vegetation product · scale factor found in prose · honest raw numbers
